problem: The sentence is broken: "u = Umax when e > 0 and u = Umin when e max the upper level (heater on)". The condition for the low output (e < 0) is missing and the words run into the definition of Umax, so the ideal law cannot be read.
fix: "An ideal two-position controller gives u = Umax when e > 0 and u = Umin when e < 0. Umax is the upper level (heater on); Umin is the lower level (heater off)."

where: Section 1, third paragraph, and Section 2, first paragraph
problem: "h is in output units, e.g. °C" and "a ... b ... in output units per minute" use "output" for the controlled variable. In this chapter u is the controller output (power, volts) and y is the temperature, so a student may read h and the rates in the wrong units.
fix: Say: "h is in the units of the error, i.e. of the measured variable, e.g. °C" and "a and b are rise and fall rates in units of the measured variable per minute, e.g. °C/min".

problem: "The slope at e = 0 is infinite and the output saturates" describes a relay as if it were a saturating proportional element. A relay has no slope at e = 0; it jumps between two fixed levels.
fix: "The output jumps between two fixed levels at e = 0, so there is no finite slope (no gain) there; the output is bounded between Umin and Umax."
